Cauchy Condensation Test

Terms get grouped into blocks that double in size here. The grouped series and the original share their fate.

For a decreasing sequence, the terms inside one block all look alike. So each block sum is trapped between multiples of one representative term. Compressing each block into its representative leaves convergence unchanged. The test becomes far easier to run.

For example, pack 🍬 candies into boxes of 1, 2, 4, doubling each time. Judging each box by one representative candy does not change whether the total is finite.

∑n≥11np converges  ⟺  p>1\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{1}{n^p}\ \text{converges} \iff p>1n≥1∑​np1​ converges⟺p>1

Use the condensation test to show that the ppp-series ∑n=1∞1np\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^p}∑n=1∞​np1​ converges for p>1p > 1p>1 and diverges for p≤1p \le 1p≤1.

Show proof

The condensed terms are Cn=2n⋅1(2n)p=2n⋅2−np=2n(1−p)=(21−p)nC_n = 2^n \cdot \frac{1}{(2^n)^p} = 2^n \cdot 2^{-np} = 2^{n(1-p)} = (2^{1-p})^nCn​=2n⋅(2n)p1​=2n⋅2−np=2n(1−p)=(21−p)n, a geometric series with ratio r=21−pr = 2^{1-p}r=21−p.

    Reindexing is also needed: the condensation in problem 1 starts at n=1n = 1n=1 and includes a C0C_0C0​ term, but this series starts at n=2n = 2n=2 and C0=10⋅ln⁡2C_0 = \frac{1}{0 \cdot \ln 2}C0​=0⋅ln21​ is singular.

    So start the condensed sum at n≥1n \ge 1n≥1 (Cn=2na2nC_n = 2^n a_{2^n}Cn​=2na2n​ with 2n≥22^n \ge 22n≥2 is well defined; finitely many terms do not affect convergence).

    Condensing with ln⁡2n=nln⁡2\ln 2^n = n \ln 2ln2n=nln2 gives Cn=2n⋅12n⋅nln⁡2=1ln⁡2⋅1nC_n = 2^n \cdot \frac{1}{2^n \cdot n \ln 2} = \frac{1}{\ln 2}\cdot\frac{1}{n}Cn​=2n⋅2n⋅nln21​=ln21​⋅n1​ for n≥1n \ge 1n≥1, so the condensed series ∑n≥1Cn\sum_{n \ge 1} C_n∑n≥1​Cn​ is 1ln⁡2\frac{1}{\ln 2}ln21​ times the harmonic series — divergent.

    Hence ∑n=2∞1nln⁡n\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n \ln n}∑n=2∞​nlnn1​ diverges too.

But bn=1n(ln⁡n)2b_n = \frac{1}{n (\ln n)^2}bn​=n(lnn)21​ also needs the decreasing verification: for x≥2x \ge 2x≥2, x(ln⁡x)2x (\ln x)^2x(lnx)2 has derivative (ln⁡x)2+2ln⁡x=ln⁡x(ln⁡x+2)>0(\ln x)^2 + 2\ln x = \ln x (\ln x + 2) > 0(lnx)2+2lnx=lnx(lnx+2)>0, so n(ln⁡n)2n (\ln n)^2n(lnn)2 is increasing and its reciprocal bnb_nbn​ is decreasing.

    Hence ∑n=2∞1n(ln⁡n)2\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n (\ln n)^2}∑n=2∞​n(lnn)21​ converges.
